SW002.finding: A 70.4% allulose syrup was followed for 16 weeks at 4-60 C. At 40 C and above, allulose declined and browning products accumulated. This is long-term syrup storage, not a baking limit.

SW003.finding: Tagatose solutions were tested at 60, 70 and 80 C. Loss was small at pH 3 but faster at pH 7, especially in phosphate buffer. The authors predicted very small loss during standard beverage pasteurization; this does not establish a baking limit.

SW011.finding: A manufacturer dossier reports 4% trehalose solution resisting hydrolysis at 100 C across pH 2-10. This is submitted product evidence, not an independently replicated baking limit.

SW013.finding: A model-solution experiment measured heat-driven HMF formation from fructose at 80, 100 and 120 C. Product formation depends on time and solution conditions; no universal sweetening limit follows.

SW014.finding: A model-solution experiment measured heat-driven HMF formation from glucose at 80, 100 and 120 C. Product formation depends on time and solution conditions; no universal sweetening limit follows.

SW015.finding: Maltose in a casein model system was studied at 120 C and pH 6.8. Isomerization, degradation and Maillard reactions occurred; results are specific to this protein-containing matrix.

SW016.finding: Lactose in a casein model system was studied at 120 C and pH 6.8. Isomerization, degradation and Maillard reactions occurred; results are specific to this protein-containing matrix.

SW017.finding: A model-solution experiment measured heat-driven HMF formation from galactose at 80, 100 and 120 C. Product formation depends on time and solution conditions; no universal sweetening limit follows.

SW019.finding: FDA describes acesulfame potassium as heat stable for baking. This supports a heat screen only; it does not replace sugar's bulk or browning role.

SW020.finding: In flavored milk, pasteurization at 90 C for 20 min caused about 40% aspartame loss; sterilization at 121 C for 15 min caused complete degradation. Loss varies with pH and matrix.

SW021.temperature_review_note: Dry sucralose started decomposing near 119 C in a laboratory test; this is not a universal food limit.
SW021.finding: FDA describes sucralose as baking-stable, while EFSA's 2026 review could not conclude on a proposed fine-bakery extension because of uncertainty about products formed under prolonged high heat. A dry-material decomposition result is not a food-matrix threshold. Keep baking use under review.

SW022.finding: FDA lists saccharin for cooking or table use, but this does not provide a matched time-temperature retention test or a universal baking threshold.

SW023.finding: In flavored milk, pasteurization at 90 C for 20 min degraded about 8% of neotame; after 121 C for 15 min about 50.5% remained. FDA nevertheless describes neotame as suitable for baking; process duration and matrix still matter.

SW024.finding: FDA describes advantame as heat stable for baking. This supports a heat screen only; it does not replace sugar's bulk or browning role.

SW025.finding: A Food Standards Australia New Zealand assessment describes cyclamate as stable in cooking and baking, without a numeric time-temperature profile. Permitted use must be checked separately for the relevant country.

SW027.finding: In soft drinks held at 80 C for 24-72 h, stevioside and Reb A degraded by up to 70%; stevioside was less stable. A separate aqueous test found 92.01% stevioside remaining after 120 C for 2 h. Matrix and duration strongly matter.

SW028.finding: In soft drinks held at 80 C for 24-72 h, stevioside and Reb A degraded by up to 70%; Reb A was more stable than stevioside. This does not establish a universal baking limit.

SW029.finding: Reb B was detected through commercial stevia extraction and purification without significant overall glycoside modification; no isolated Reb B baking time-temperature test was established.

SW030.finding: Reb C was detected through commercial stevia extraction and purification without significant overall glycoside modification; no isolated Reb C baking time-temperature test was established.

SW031.finding: Reb D was identified in commercial stevia end product after processing, but the study does not give an isolated Reb D food-heating limit.

SW033.finding: Reb F was detected through commercial stevia extraction and purification without significant overall glycoside modification; no isolated Reb F baking time-temperature test was established.

SW034.finding: An aqueous test found 94.07% Reb M remaining after 120 C for 2 h. This tested formulation and duration do not define a universal baking maximum.

SW038.finding: Dulcoside A was detected through commercial stevia extraction and purification without significant overall glycoside modification; no isolated cooking limit was established.

SW039.finding: Rubusoside was detected through commercial stevia extraction and purification without significant overall glycoside modification; no isolated cooking limit was established.

SW040.finding: Steviolbioside was detected through commercial stevia extraction and purification without significant overall glycoside modification; no isolated cooking limit was established.

SW041.finding: In monk-fruit extract, mogroside V retention was 99.9% at 90 C for 2 h and 95.1% at 120 C for 2 h. Extract composition matters; this is not a pure-compound or universal baking limit.

SW042.finding: Mogroside IV content changed when whole monk fruit was dried at 40-80 C. Biosynthesis and interconversion may contribute; no isolated mogroside IV heat limit was established.

SW043.finding: Mogroside III content changed when whole monk fruit was dried at 40-80 C. This cannot be translated into an isolated-compound cooking limit.

SW044.finding: Mogroside IIe content changed when whole monk fruit was dried at 40-80 C. This cannot be translated into an isolated-compound cooking limit.

SW045.finding: Siamenoside I in acidic mock beverages at pH 2.8-4.2 and 5-40 C over 26 weeks lost about 2% at the harshest tested condition (pH 2.8, 40 C). This is storage evidence, not baking evidence.

SW046.finding: 11-Oxo-mogroside V content changed when whole monk fruit was dried at 40-80 C. This cannot be translated into an isolated-compound cooking limit.

SW047.finding: A stability-indicating HPLC study stressed glycyrrhizin at 80 C for 24 h and reported comparatively greater stability under the tested thermal condition. It did not establish sweetness retention in food.

SW048.finding: Neohesperidin dihydrochalcone in diluted aqueous solutions was tested at 50, 70 and 90 C. Degradation followed pH-dependent first-order kinetics, with best stability near pH 4.5; no universal baking limit follows.

SW057.finding: Thaumatin loses sweetness by aggregation when heated near neutral/basic pH; acidic conditions slow the loss. A primary study reports loss above about 70 C near neutral pH, so food pH is essential.

SW058.finding: Native two-chain monellin loses sweetness as temperature rises in aqueous heating experiments; heat-related chain dissociation makes it unsuitable for an unqualified baking pass. Engineered single-chain variants are different substances.

SW059.finding: Original brazzein study found sweetness was not destroyed by 80 C for 4 h. A newer study examined structural inactivation at 80-100 C for 2 h; this does not give a universal oven limit.

SW060.finding: A protein-engineering study measured the low thermal stability of wild-type neoculin and raised its melting temperature with mutations. A melting temperature is not a food-processing or sweetness-retention limit.

SW061.finding: Curculin taste-modifying activity was unchanged after 50 C for 1 h over pH 3-11 in the tested solution. Higher-temperature baking performance was not shown.

SW064.finding: An early experiment found both thaumatin I and II eventually lose sweetness on heating due to irreversible conformational change. An acidic-matrix report describes thaumatin II retaining sweetness at 80 C for 4 h at pH 2; neither gives a general baking limit.

SW065.finding: Fresh miracle-fruit pulp heated for 5 min kept function at 40-45 C, lost some at 50 C, and lost taste-modifying function at 60-70 C. The result concerns pulp rather than purified miraculin.

ING004.finding: Tested monk-fruit extract retained mogroside V at 90 C for 2 h (99.9%) and 120 C for 2 h (95.1%). A different extract may behave differently.

ING005.finding: Tested mogroside-V-containing monk-fruit extract retained mogroside V at 90 C for 2 h (99.9%) and 120 C for 2 h (95.1%). Verify the actual product composition before transferring this result.
